C08-M03-L02-F1.title: The parser as a decision pipeline
C08-M03-L02-F1.caption: How a parser handles every event, and why each branch ends in storage with a label rather than deletion.
C08-M03-L02-F1.alt: Graph diagram, top to bottom. Raw event + source type leads to Select parser, then to the decision Header matches?. No leads to Unparsed: _parse_failure (original kept). Yes leads to Extract + convert (fields, types, UTC time), then to the decision Required fields present?. All leads to Parsed event + raw; some missing leads to Partial: _parse_warning. All three outcomes lead to Stored and counted. A dashed arrow labelled failure count goes from Unparsed: _parse_failure to Parser health dashboard.
C08-M03-L02-F1.note: No branch deletes the event: failures are labelled, kept and counted.

C08-M03-L02-F2.title: Brittle versus tolerant firewall parser
C08-M03-L02-F2.caption: The kit demo's positional regex against a header regex with key-value lookup, with the results each produced on the same variant lines.
C08-M03-L02-F2.alt: Two code panels. Left, red, Brittle: one positional regex. The pattern requires SRC, DST, PROTO=(\w+) DPT=(\d+) in fixed order; the code uses m[1] without checking for a match. Results: ICMP with no port, keys reordered and new [FW-IN] prefix all fail with TypeError; parsed 2 of 5. Right, green, Tolerant: header regex + key-value. An anchored header with an optional [prefix]; if no match, return a _parse_failure tag with the original; kv = dict of key=value tokens; fields read with kv.get; the port is added only if present. Results: all 4 firewall drops parsed; link-down line tagged _parse_failure.
C08-M03-L02-F2.note: Parse by label, check every match, and tag failures instead of crashing.
